final:
I saved the sequence diagram to `docs/checkout-flow.md` and changed no code. The junior-dev review didn't give a real check of the diagram.

The diagram follows `place_order` in `src/app.py` and `charge` in `src/payments.py`:
1. Stock is checked for each item. If any item is short, the order is rejected and nothing is charged.
2. The card is charged for the total, which is price times quantity per item, in cents. A failed charge rejects the order.
3. Stock is reduced, then the order is appended to `data/orders.json` and returned as placed.

It has short notes on the main points:
- The check happens before the charge.
- Stock only lives in memory.
- Order ids are the number of existing orders plus one.

**README mismatch:** `README.md` mentions `POST /orders` and an emailed receipt. The code has no HTTP route and sends no email, so I left both out and said so in the notes.

# shopfront

A tiny order service used as the fixture for Junior-dev's headless runs. Customers place
orders through `POST /orders`; the service checks stock, charges the card through the
payment provider, and records the order. Orders are kept in `data/orders.json`.

Run it with `python -m src.app`. It needs no database. You will recieve an email receipt

# Checkout flow

How `place_order(customer, items, card_token)` in `src/app.py` works.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor C as Customer
    participant A as app.place_order
    participant S as STOCK (in memory)
    participant P as payments.charge
    participant F as data/orders.json

    C->>A: customer, items, card_token
    loop each item
        A->>S: enough stock?
    end
    Note over A,S: Any shortfall stops here. Nothing is charged.
    alt out of stock
        A-->>C: rejected ("out of stock: <item>")
    else all in stock
        A->>P: charge(card_token, total)
        Note over A,P: total = sum of PRICES x qty, in cents
        P-->>A: {ok, id}
        alt payment failed (e.g. empty token)
            A-->>C: rejected ("payment failed")
        else payment ok
            A->>S: subtract ordered quantities
            Note over S: Stock lives in memory only. A restart resets it.
            A->>F: read orders, append order, write file
            Note over F: id = number of existing orders + 1
            A-->>C: placed (order with payment id)
        end
    end
```

## Notes

- Stock is checked before the card is charged, so out-of-stock orders are never billed.
- Stock is only reduced after payment succeeds.
- The README mentions `POST /orders` and an emailed receipt. `src/app.py` has no HTTP route and sends no email, so neither appears in the diagram.
